subject: Request: DPIA support + sample logs for cross-border transfer review
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@swiftbank.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03 09:12 PST
Subject: Request: DPIA support and sample logs for cross-border transfer review

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking this — SwiftBank is starting a targeted DPIA and cross-border transfer review for a new payments integration. We need Redwood to provide a small set of artifacts so our privacy and legal teams can complete the assessment and confirm lawful transfer mechanisms. Can you provide the following by COB Nov 10?

- Export of the Art. 30 processing register excerpt relevant to the SwiftBank integration (fields: processing purpose, categories of data, recipients, legal basis, retention).
- Current list of active subprocessors with contact + country of operation and contract date.
- A redacted sample (7–10 rows) of access logs showing read/access events for records associated with the SwiftBank tenant (timestamp, role, region, action).
- Confirmation of transfer mechanisms in use (SCCs, standard contractual terms, or adequacy + any supplementary controls).
- KMS key lineage reference (not the raw key) and whether customer data blobs are encrypted at rest + in transit.

We can accept redacted samples and pre-signed links to S3 exports. Please also include a short attestation page (one para) signed by your compliance lead confirming the samples are representative and that PII has been redacted.

Attached is a short request packet with our preferred format (SwiftBank_DPIA_Request.pdf). If you prefer, we can run a 30-minute kickoff to agree scope — are you available tomorrow (Nov 4) after 10am PST?

Best,
Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of Privacy Operations
SwiftBank

---
Attachment: SwiftBank_DPIA_Request.pdf (pdf, 84KB)
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@swiftbank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-03 11:02 PST
Subject: Re: Request: DPIA support and sample logs for cross-border transfer review

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Marcus here (Head of Customer Security at Redwood). We can support this request and will scope the artifacts to minimize exposure while giving you what you need for the DPIA. Proposed plan:

1) Art.30 extract: we'll pull the processing activities for the SwiftBank integration only and include the mapping fields you list.
2) Subprocessor table: curated list with country and onboarding date; we'll include contract references (DPA addendum id).
3) Access logs: provide a redacted sample of up to 10 events (ISO timestamps) showing access patterns; we'll redact any full identifiers and provide a mapping key offline if needed.
4) Transfer mechanisms & KMS: statement of mechanisms in use plus KMS lineage reference (no raw keys).
5) Attestation: we will provide a one-paragraph signed attestation from our Privacy officer.

Karthik (cc) will own the access-log extraction; Marissa will coordinate documents and the attestation. Would a 30-minute call tomorrow Nov 4 at 11:00am PST work to finalize the sample format? If not, we can use the drive link you provided.

I attached a short evidence scope template (rdwd_evidence_scope_v1.xlsx) that shows fields we'll export. We'll flag any items that need legal redaction.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: rdwd_evidence_scope_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

Subject: Re: Request: DPIA support and sample logs for cross-border transfer review

Marcus / Marissa — quick technical note on feasibility and suggested delivery format.

- We can produce the Art.30 extract from our governance DB (export filters: customer_id=swiftbank, service_scope=payments). That will include purpose, categories, recipients, legal basis, retention.
- For access-logs: the prod cluster logs are in eu-west-1 and stored in an S3 partition. I recommend: run a query to extract the minimal event attributes, redact user identifiers, and provide a pre-signed S3 URL to a zipped CSV. Sample size: 7 rows is fine for the DPIA; more if they request patterns.
- Subprocessor inventory: current inventory table includes vendor_id, country, contract_date, and DPA_addendum_id. We can include the DPA addendum id but not the full contract PDF unless they sign an NDA or DocuSign permission.
- KMS: we can provide key alias, rotation cadence, and whether envelope encryption is used — legal will need to confirm whether sharing key aliases is allowed.

Attached are two snippets I plan to run to generate the sample (log_query_snippets.txt). I'll coordinate with infra to get pre-signed URLs and will stage them in a restricted drive folder.

Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Security
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: log_query_snippets.txt (txt, 3KB)

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed plan. Nov 10 is OK on our side but we would appreciate the initial artifacts sooner if possible. A couple of follow-ups:

- Please include a brief attestation letter from Redwood Privacy (one paragraph) confirming samples are representative.
- Could you include a single-line reference to the DPA clause you intend to rely on for processors (e.g., DPA Addendum, Clause 5.2 or equivalent)? That helps our legal mapping.
- We'll open a Jira for internal tracking: JIRA-SEC-1122. Please paste any pre-signed links and ticket updates there.

If you can get the Art.30 extract + subprocessor table by Nov 8, and the redacted log sample + attestation by Nov 10, that would be perfect. Thanks again — we may need a short confirmation from your legal team about whether the DPA addendum can be included in our evidence packet; if so we'll request a redacted PDF.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Head of Privacy Operations
SwiftBank
